{"name": "charge-review", "steps": "Inputs: the developer's org or account id, the invoice (id or month), the lines and amounts they mean, request ids if they have them.

1. Identify the account. If you have neither org nor account id, ask_developer for org_id (plus invoice_id/invoice_month and line_items/amounts/request_ids in the same call if not given). lookup_account.
2. Check billing channel, plan and has_signed_contract on the account.
   - Not billed directly by Redwood: search_knowledge for the procedure for that exact channel (cloud marketplace vs reseller are different pages; apply only the one matching billing_channel). Support credits/disputes nothing there; tell the developer who bills them and where refunds/credits/invoices go. Open a case only if the current page says so (e.g. a metering mismatch).
3. get_invoice (map a month to an id from lookup_account's invoice list). Read console_confirmed_duplicates (original_line vs copy_lines, decided by where the usage records point), same_requests_but_unconfirmed, and same_amount_but_different_requests. get_usage for request ids the developer gave.
4. Classify:
   a. Console-confirmed duplicate: act only on the copy line, never the original.
   b. Look-alike (same amount/description, different request ids), no second line, or usage pointing to neither/both lines: NOT a confirmed duplicate. Say so plainly with the console evidence. Never say a credit is likely before the console confirms a duplicate.
   c. Wrong rate/quantity/product, unrecognized usage, retries/cancelled streams, token mismatch: search the usage/token pages; if they explain it, explain and stop.
   d. Waive/reduce a correct charge (goodwill, exception, SLA credit, refund): not Support's to issue. Load team-handoff.
5. For (a), search_knowledge for what Support may do now: the Support charter (which accounts Support may credit at all), the credits-and-disputes page, and Finance's approval matrix for the per-line limit. The limit can depend on how the invoice was rated (e.g. which price book applies to the invoice's usage period): search the Finance close calendar for that, using the invoice period. Drafts, proposals and threads change nothing.
   - Support may credit this account and the copy line's full amount is within the limit: confirm_with_developer "I'll issue a credit note of $X (full amount) on the duplicated line L of invoice I." Only after yes: issue_credit_note (reason duplicate, memo with request ids). Tell them the credit note id and amount, and when it applies if the page says. No handoff.
   - Over the limit, or an account Support may not credit (e.g. contract/enterprise per the charter): do not credit or split. confirm_with_developer "I'll open a dispute on line L of invoice I (duplicate charge, request ids R) and hand it to Billing Ops." After yes: open_dispute, then load team-handoff and escalate with the dispute id.
   - If the developer says no: write nothing (no credit, dispute or case); say nothing was changed and they can come back.
6. For (b) and unexplained (c): gather intake (invoice, both lines, window in the account's billing timezone, request ids, what they checked) with ask_developer, then load team-handoff.
7. Never promise a dispute outcome or date. If a write is rejected, read get_invoice to see the state before saying anything."}

description: Summary:
We observed a class of meter/accounting mismatches where token usage emitted to billing was lower than the actual tokens served when requests were routed to fallback model variants. This manifests as undercharging for customers and incorrect per-route quota enforcement (routes appear to consume fewer tokens than expected).
Observed behavior:
- Primary route (route-A) is configured with model M1. body: ## Purpose
The support console can look up a customer's billing account, issue a credit note against invoice lines, and open a billing dispute. This page defines when Support uses each one. It amends the billing routing page for duplicate charges only; everything else on that page still applies. This version is effective from 26 February 2027 and adds how to tell the copy from the original. Support's per-line limit is set in Finance's Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix (Finance shared drive), which FP&A revised in February 2027; check the matrix for the limit that applies to the invoice in front of you."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-console-duplicate-charges-and-disputes-2027.json", "chunk": "7/7", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes (v2)", "status": "published", "date": "2027-02-26", "text": "## Common mistakes
- Crediting the original line instead of the copy.
- Crediting a line because two lines share a description or an amount, without matching request IDs.
- Splitting a line over the limit into several credits.
- Crediting a marketplace purchase: the marketplace bills those, so Support has nothing to credit.
- Telling the customer a dispute will succeed, or when Billing Ops will finish.
## Questions
Ask in #support-billing. Page owner: Dev Patel.

body: Overview
Purpose: This cookbook defines a pragmatic, repeatable approach for mapping customer-visible telemetry to clear owners, creating routing rules in our alerting stack, and operationalizing those alerts inside Customer Success (CS) and Engineering workflows. It is intended for CS onboarding leads, SREs, and product owners who need consistent, auditable alerts that drive fast, customer-facing outcomes.
Scope: applies to all enterprise tenants (hosted, dedicated, private) and the following telemetry sources: telemetry-gateway, redwood-proxy, model-router, kvcache-service, embeddings-indexer. This doc focuses on customer-impacting metrics (latency, error-rate, cost-anomaly, model-quality regression) rather than internal infra-only metrics.
Owner and Contact
- Primary owner: Customer Success Observability (team-ops-cs-observability)"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/hosted-api-packages-free-tier-and-overage-policy.json", "chunk": "13/16", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Hosted API Packages: Free Tier, Included Usage, and Overage Policy", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-26", "text": "## Packaging enforcement rules (implementation policy)

   - Clear “effective date” and a customer comms plan if externally visible
3) Any experiment that changes packaging must tag cohorts in analytics and be reported with pre/post segmentation if meter fixes overlap.

{"query": "billed tokens canonical accounting rules tokenizer payload tool calls structured output retries idempotency usage metering details hosted API", "results": [{"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/hosted-api-packages-free-tier-and-overage-policy.json", "chunk": "6/16", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Hosted API Packages: Free Tier, Included Usage, and Overage Policy", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-26", "text": "### What counts toward billed tokens
Counts toward billed tokens:
- Prompt tokens that are processed for a request
- Completion tokens successfully generated and delivered (including streamed tokens that were sent before a disconnect)
- Tool/function call tokens and structured output tokens that are part of the model’s generated output (see meter spec)
Does NOT count toward billed tokens:
- Non-billable internal retries that are deduped by idempotency keys
- Requests rejected before model execution due to auth failure, invalid params, or quota pre-check (typically 4xx)"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/gcp-marketplace-sku-and-billing-dimensions.json", "chunk": "7/18", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "GCP Marketplace: SKU & Billing Dimensions (v2)", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-20", "text": "(continued) ### Hosted API (usage-based) dimensions
- “Tokens” are counted using the serving model’s tokenizer, consistent with Redwood API usage analytics.
- For multi-part requests (tool calls, structured output), token counting follows the same accounting as existing Redwood hosted billing.
- If a request fails before inference begins (e.g., auth/validation), no usage is reported.
- If inference begins and fails mid-stream, usage is based on tokens actually generated and delivered (best effort); partial tokens are included."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/hosted-api-packages-free-tier-and-overage-policy.json", "chunk": "12/16", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Hosted API Packages: Free Tier, Included Usage, and Overage Policy", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-26", "text": "### Avoid / do not say
- “We bill on raw tokens.”
- “Retries are always free.” (Only true if deduped and classified non-billable.)
- “Cache hits don’t count.” (Not true by default.)
- “Token counts match OpenAI exactly.” (We align semantics, but do not promise identical counts across providers.)
### If asked: “Why do billed tokens differ from my local tokenizer?”
Approved response:
- “Tokenization can vary across libraries and model families. Redwood reports **billed tokens** using our canonical tokenization and accounting rules, and we expose that same number consistently across the Console, Usage API, and invoices.”

1. If a report arrives in Slack or Gmail, file a SUP ticket and link it.
2. Mark the SUP ticket label `token-accounting` and add the origin channel in the description (Slack/Gmail).
3. In weekly reporting, count the case by *origin* (Slack vs Gmail vs Jira), not by total artifacts.
## Common root causes to check
- Streaming retries/reconnect (tokens can be emitted twice)
- Client counts only final chunk tokens
- Different tokenizer / unicode normalization
- Whitespace/newlines included in input strings
- Tool-call serialization adds tokens
- Prefix-cache billing bug (rare; see SUP-3009)"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/token-accounting-discrepancy-intake-and-triage.json", "chunk": "4/4", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Ops: Reconciling token accounting discrepancy reports (intake + triage)", "status": "published", "date": "2025-04-22", "text": "## Known examples (for reference)

KPI: Blended $/1M Output Tokens
* Non-GPU costs (e.g., general SaaS tools) unless included as a fixed overhead allocation in the finance methodology
* One-time credits/promotions (these affect revenue/billing, not cost)
h4. Denominator: Output tokens
*Output tokens* are the platform-metered tokens generated by the model as completion output.
Inclusions:
* Tokens produced in non-streaming responses
* Tokens produced in streaming responses (requires parity across streaming code paths)
Exclusions/notes:
* Input/prompt tokens are *not* in the denominator for this KPI (v1 is output-token-centric for comparability across workloads).
* Tool call payload tokens are included only if they are counted by the canonical tokenizer in the serving path; v1 will follow metering standard and document known edge cases.
* Truncation behavior must be consistent: count tokens actually emitted to the client (or logically generated if streaming partial emissions are retried), per metering spec.

Dimensions (grouping keys)"}, {"source": "sources/gmail/rachel_kim/20250509-billing-attribution-system-tool-clarify.json", "chunk": "4/9", "kind": "email thread", "title": "Billing attribution for system prompts and tool outputs — clarification requested", "status": "n/a", "date": "2025-05-15", "text": "Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear examples. Short answers up front, then a worked example:
Policy summary (current Redwood hosted API billing):
- System messages are tokenized and counted as input tokens each time they are sent to the model, unless you use the \"service-side\" system override that pins the system prompt server-side for the session (not available by default). In your case, because the system content is included in each request, it is billed as input.
- Tool-return content: when a tool is invoked and the tool returns text that the model incorporates into its final output, the tool-return tokens are billed as OUTPUT tokens. If a tool return is resubmitted as input for a subsequent model call, those tokens would also be billed again as input on that subsequent call.
- Rounding: Redwood token accounting does per-request tokenization with integer token counts (no fractional tokens). We round up token math per request (i.e., each request's pre- and post-token counts are integerized, then aggregated on the invoice). There is no extra per-tool rounding beyond that."}]}

{"name": "team-handoff", "steps": "1. Decide whether a case is needed at all. search_knowledge for the routing policy covering this request (e.g. "billing case routing <topic>", "who approves <request>"). If a current page says Support answers this without a case (an explanation, a general rule, a self-service step, "your account team confirms your terms", a known delay or threshold not yet reached, a failure inside a published incident window), answer and stop.
2. Pick the owning team from the current routing/approval/charter documents, not from drafts, proposals or chat threads. Use the console account (plan, channel, contracts) to choose between rows, e.g. self-serve vs signed contract, direct vs marketplace. If the developer claims something the console doesn't show (a contract, a plan), route per the policy for that situation.
3. Collect the intake the receiving team needs (the routing page lists it per row) with one ask_developer call: e.g. invoice_id, line_items, amounts, request_ids, time_of_issue together with timezone, error_code, checks_done, contract. Give windows in the account's billing_timezone (convert from what the developer said). If they don't have something, hand off anyway and record it as "not provided".
4. Do any permitted credit or dispute first (each needs the developer's explicit yes), because escalation closes the console. A plain handoff needs no confirmation.
5. escalate_case with: team; priority as the current pages say (normal for billing handoffs unless the routing page says urgent); summary (what they asked, what the console shows, what the team must decide/do); details with every fact given (ids, amounts as the console shows them, window in billing timezone, request ids, amount requested if any, what's missing); dispute_id if any. Never card numbers; if one was shared, write "customer shared a card number (removed)".
6. Tell the developer: anything the policy row says to tell the customer (e.g. a rule for their plan or channel), which team has it, the case id, and what that team will do next. No promised outcome, amount or date; no internal credit tables or ranges."}

arguments.summary: Orchard Metrics asked Redwood to check unusually high billed tokens for req_o81 and req_o82 in August 2026 usage. Console shows both successful requests on the August direct Hosted Self-Serve invoice line, billed at 4,100,000 and 3,900,000 tokens, respectively. The developer reports the complete payloads, including tool definitions, tokenize to about 41,000 tokens each using Redwood's tokenize endpoint and says neither request was retried. Please investigate meter correctness for these requests and route any necessary billing correction to Billing Ops; no correction or credit has been made.
